outcome: Composite wound morbidity (wound separation, infection, dehiscence)
Individual components of composite wound morbidity
cohort: 3,901 morbidly obese women (BMI ≥ 40) who underwent cesarean delivery between July 2012 and May 2019
finding: The study found no significant difference in the frequency of composite wound morbidity between Pfannenstiel and vertical skin incisions overall, but infraumbilical vertical skin incision was associated with increased wound morbidity and infection compared to Pfannenstiel incision.
